In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human gastrocnemic muscle tendon unit operates as a spring during the stance phase of walking.

the muscle and tendon operate in parallel during walking, each contributing to locomotor economy in different ways, with the muscle operating in an isometric mode and the tendon behaving like a spring.
the behaviour of the muscle and the tendon is a combination of the two mechanisms, which are not mutually exclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human muscle tendon unit is an efficient structure for locomotion, with the muscle and tendon playing different but complementary roles.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the muscle fascicles operate at a relatively constant length during stance phase and the tendon stores and releases elastic strain energy during walking.

, although the muscle fascicles operate at relatively short lengths during walking, the musculotendinous complex is able to produce the forces required to move the body at a speed of 3 km h1 by means of a combination of active muscle shortening and tendon stretch.
